# Native-secret cloud execution (no manuscript work)

The approved five-seed programme is implemented by `tools/finish_five_seed.py`.
The workflow **Authorized five-seed research through real results** is an
optional cloud coordinator around that same tested entrypoint. It does not
change prompts, scores, references, model settings or the statistical unit.

## Native credential prerequisite

`GEMINI_API_KEY` and the original `AUTHOR_REVIEW_AES_KEY_BASE64` must be native
repository Actions secrets. A chat attachment does not set a repository secret.
Never commit a key, publish an encrypted-secret workaround, or log a key value.
The key is authenticated against the existing original archive before a cloud
execution lease or any model request is created. Missing secrets stop immediately.

## Execution, persistence and continuation

On initial execution the coordinator performs all real qualification and
full-cohort mock tests, verifies original private references, creates a new
unsigned technical freeze and binds the user's already recorded delegation to
separate main and ablation scope records. It then executes main, all five
ablations, isolated judging and actual paired analysis. There are no new blanket
approval prompts, forged signatures or altered gold references.

Each invocation permits up to 100 new requests/packets per phase. Re-entry
replays recorded responses only; failed or ambiguous protected requests are
never resent. Successful safe checkpoints automatically dispatch the next
workflow only after there is durable progress. A genuine error, no progress,
incomplete checkpoint, or completed experiment stops automatic continuation.
This is workflow continuation, not an inference retry.

The branch `execution-state/five-seed-v1` records a compare-and-swap execution
lease and the latest encrypted checkpoint identity. It contains no reference
answers, private result rows, keys or signatures. Every continuation checks out
the original claimed commit and restores the latest checkpoint. A claim left
unresolved by runner interruption blocks new execution; **do not delete/reset
it or use an older checkpoint to evade the no-reroll rule**. Investigate the
exact failed job and its durable evidence first.

Checkpoints include the original and failed raw outputs, requests, receipts,
freeze, authorization, metrics and resumable controller state. Original review
files are independently restored from their existing encrypted archive. Only an
AES-GCM-encrypted ZIP and nonsecret integrity metadata are uploaded as artifacts.
The same original archive key is used with a fresh random nonce and authenticated
checkpoint-purpose/source-commit header. Native credentials and local key files
are excluded. The original research archive is never re-encrypted or changed.

The cloud wrapper, workflow and tests live under `.github/` and are bound by the
immutable claimed Git commit; the scientific protocol separately binds the
research/tool/test inventories, dependencies and real evidence. Python is pinned
to the qualified 3.11.17 interpreter. Runtime/configuration drift fails closed.

## Starting and observing

After the native secrets are configured, run the workflow from Actions on main.
The main merge also triggers its first prerequisite check. No protected calls
can occur when the archive secret is missing. Code success or a saved checkpoint
is **not** a claim of completed benchmark results. Completion is reported only
after the existing independent result verifier accepts the real main and ablation
archives and their judgments; unresolved judgments remain explicit bounds.

Cloud execution can span multiple jobs/days under the existing API ceilings.
Provider failures, daily quotas, Actions/storage limits, or a runner timeout can
still require inspection. After a new checkpoint is uploaded and its pointer committed, duplicate encrypted
archives older than the latest two may be deleted; all original and failed
request records remain in both cumulative snapshots. Artifacts expire after
14 days; preserve the final
verified encrypted results securely. Do not describe elapsed-time estimates as
guarantees or automatically reissue unknown requests after a timeout.
